options.name: Display / programmatic ads
options.description: An ad network auctions banner slots on your pages and pays per impression. AdSense has no traffic minimum; Mediavine's Journey tier starts around 1,000 monthly sessions; Raptive from ~25,000 pageviews with mostly tier-1 traffic. Premium networks typically pay $15-35 RPM.

options.name: Direct banner sales
options.description: Selling a fixed banner slot straight to one sponsor for a flat monthly fee - no network cut, full control of the creative. The marketingShark devShark banner infrastructure is the in-house precursor.
blockers: Needs an audience number to price against

options.name: Newsletter / edition sponsorship
options.description: A sponsor pays a flat fee for a labelled slot in the daily edition. The trend is toward integrated, trust-based placements over one-off generic ads; newsletter ad networks (e.g. beehiiv's) pay out over $1M/month to publishers, or you sell direct.

options.name: Affiliate links (AI tools / SaaS)
options.description: You recommend a product with a tracked link; when a reader buys or subscribes through it, the merchant pays a commission - SaaS programs often pay 20-30% recurring. Natural fit for an AI magazine that already covers tools.

options.name: Affiliate links (gear / Amazon)
options.description: The same model pointed at physical goods - MMA gloves, apparel, books - through Amazon Associates or brand programs. Low rates (1-10%) but near-zero effort once links live in article templates.

options.name: Betting affiliate (CPA / RevShare)
options.description: Sportsbooks pay per referred depositor (CPA), a share of their revenue (RevShare), or a hybrid. The highest-paying niche open to MMA and fight-prediction content - and the most regulated: Czech rules require the Ministry of Finance addiction warning, 18+ labelling and gambling-ad compliance; Meta requires special authorisation for betting ads.

options.name: Print-on-demand merch
options.description: A POD partner (Printful, Printify, Gelato) holds blank garments; when a customer orders your design they print and ship a single unit. No inventory, no upfront cost - you keep the markup over the base price. Gelato fulfils locally in 32 countries, strong for the EU. This is exactly the Titty Tuesdays model.

options.name: Dropshipping
options.description: You list a third-party supplier's generic product in your store; when someone buys, the supplier ships it directly and you keep the price difference. Unlike POD the product is not your design - thin margins, no differentiation, quality risk. POD is the better fit for a design-led brand.

options.name: Paid newsletter tier
options.description: A premium edition readers pay monthly for while the daily stays free. Paid newsletter subscriptions have roughly tripled since 2021; on beehiiv, subscription revenue grew 138% in a year and about 30% of revenue-generating creators earn through paid tiers.

options.name: Premium picks subscription
options.description: Selling FightAIQ's model output (picks, probabilities, closing-line analysis) as a paid subscription. Needs a public, verifiable track record first - the backtest receipts are what makes this credible.

options.name: Membership / supporter tier
options.description: Recurring supporter payments (community access, early access, name in credits) via Ko-fi, Buy Me a Coffee memberships or Memberful. Lighter than a paid newsletter - perks, not paywalled content.

options.name: Productized service
options.description: A fixed-scope, fixed-price service: e.g. a branded 8-slide carousel in 48 hours powered by the Design Lab, or a GoVIRAL content brief for a client's account. Sells the system's output as a service without custom scoping.

options.name: Data / API licensing
options.description: Licensing structured data the system already maintains - fight datasets, model probabilities - as a paid API or bulk-export subscription for other sites and researchers.
blockers: Licence terms need a legal look

options.name: Content syndication / licensing
options.description: Other outlets pay to republish articles or the daily briefing (including AI-training licensing for a clean, well-structured archive). Value grows with archive size and the citation discipline the truth gates already enforce.

options.name: Donations / tip jar
options.description: A Ko-fi or Buy Me a Coffee link on the site. Zero setup cost, small but immediate; the honest baseline while everything else waits on audience size.

options.name: Niche job board
options.description: Companies pay to list roles in front of a niche audience - the classic AI-newsletter adjacency: an AI-jobs board beside the daily briefing. Needs steady traffic to be worth a listing fee.
